div.l: The ȝonge gerles / of the diocise
And knew her consaill ⁊and what was al her rede
A garland hadde he / sette vpon his hede
As grete as it were / for an ale stake
A bokeler hadde he / made hym of a cake
With hym ther roode / a gentil pardoner
Of Rouncyvall / his freend and his comper
That streight was come / fro the court of Rome
Ful lowde he song / come hider loue to me
This sompnoᵘur bar to hym / a stif burdoıı̄un
Was neủere trompe / of half so greet a soıı̄un
This ꝑpardoner hadde heer / as ȝelwe as wax
But smothe it heeng / as doth a strike of flax
By ounces henge his lokkes / that he hadde
And ther with he / his shuldres oủerspradde
But thynne it lay / by culpıı̄uns oon and oon
But hood for iolyte / wered he noon
For it was trussed / vp in his walet
Him thoughte he rood / al on the newe iet
Discheuele saaf his cappe / he rood al bare
Suche glaringe eyen / hadde he as an hare
A vernicle hadde he / sewed vpon his cappe
His walet lay bifore hym / in his lappe
Bretfull of pardoıı̄un comen fro Rome al hoot
A voys he hadde / as smal as a goot
No berde ne hadde he / ne neủere shulde haue
As smothe it was / as it ware late shaue
I trowe he were a geldyng or a mare
But of his craft / fro Berwyk in to Ware
Ne was ther such / another ꝑpardoner
For in his male / he hadde a pilweber
Wich that he seide / was oure lady veyl
He seide he hadde a gobet of the seyl
That seint petre hadde / whan þᵗat he wente
Vp on the see / til ihu crist hym hente
He hadde a cros of latoıı̄un / ful of stones
And in a glas / he hadde pigges bones
But with thise relikes / whan that he fond
A poủere ꝑpersoıı̄un / dwellynge vp on lond
